To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a mutation in the gene encoding TBC1D 1, an insulin signaling protein, is responsible for the leanness of a lean mouse strain, and that this mutation increases fatty acid oxidation in skeletal muscle and thereby reduces body weight.

we have identified the first obesity-suppressing gene from the Swiss Jim Lambert (lean) mouse strain and that the mutation of this gene, Tbc1d, suppresses obesity by increasing lipid oxidation in skeletal muscle.
a single gene mutation, Tbc1d11 in the mouse, causes leanness and protects against diet-induced obesity by increasing lipid oxidation and decreasing glucose uptake in skeletal muscle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genes and pathways involved in the regulation of body weight and energy balance.
the identification of genes involved in the regulation of obesity and the elucidation of their molecular function.
the identification of genes and pathways involved in obesity, diabetes and related metabolic diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TBC1D11 is a novel obesity gene and that TBC1d1 is a novel obesity suppressor.
TBC1D is an insulin-regulated protein that plays a critical role in the control of glucose and lipid metabolism and that mutations in the gene are associated with obesity in humans and mice.
the SJL-specific Tbc1d mutation is responsible for the leanness of SJL mice and that this mutation is a suppressor of obesity and diabetes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Tbc1d11 mutation in the SJL strain confers leannes and protects from diet induced obesity.
a mutation in a protein related to insulin signaling in skeletal muscle is responsible for a genetic difference that confers leanness.
the SJL strain carries a mutation in the TBC1D gene that confers leanness to the mice and protects against diet-induced obesity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single gene mutation in the TBC1D family can suppress obesity by increasing the use of lipids in skeletal muscle.
TBC1D proteins are important regulators of lipid metabolism in skeletal muscle.
the Tbc1D1 mutation is a key genetic factor that protects SJL mice from high-fat diet– and obesity-induced insulin resistance and diabetes.
